title: Technical Documentation
summary: Practice recording technical observations so another person can understand what happened.
objectives: Create a concise technical observation record.
Separate symptoms, evidence, actions, and outcomes.

vocab.def: An event that affects or may affect a system or service.
A recorded fact noticed during an investigation.
What happened after an action or event.

sections.heading: Write for the next person
sections.body: A useful record includes date and time, system, observation, symptom, evidence, action attempted, and outcome. Clear records help a team compare events instead of relying on memory.

sections.heading: Facts and assumptions differ
sections.body: 'Network status changed to warning at 10:15' is an observation. 'The switch failed' is a possible cause that needs evidence. Labeling the difference improves troubleshooting.

sections.heading: Document a synthetic event
sections.body: Use a provided scenario and complete a short incident record. Do not record real student data, production telemetry, credentials, or private infrastructure details.

practice.prompt: Rewrite 'the server was broken' as a record containing time, system, observable symptom, evidence, action, and outcome.

quiz.question: Which statement is an observation?
options: Network status changed to warning at 10:15
The next incident will never happen
quiz.answer: Network status changed to warning at 10:15

lab.objective: Complete a technical record from a synthetic incident scenario.

reflectionPrompt: What makes a technical note useful to someone who was not present?
